title: Establish trust (share CAs)
breadcrumb: Federation Hub: connecting multiple TAK Servers

headings.text: The two CAs to exchange, per deployment
When mTLS isn't possible: token auth

blocks.html:
The hub authenticates connections with X.509 mutual TLS, so the hub and each TAK Server must trust each other's Certificate Authority (CA). On Deploy App this matters because each deployment has its own CA (Legacy/Docker stacks use CFSSL; Kubernetes uses opendefence-pki) — there's no shared trust until you create it.

Run unique certificates per server. Sharing one CA across deployments makes the hub treat them as interconnected (see policy) and share everything — the opposite of controlled federation.

The two CAs to exchange, per deployment

For each Deploy App TAK Server you connect:

  1. Give the hub the server's CA. Each TAK Server's CA is at /opt/tak/certs/files/ca.pem. In the hub UI's Certificate Manager (CA Manager), Choose File → Upload it. It's added to the hub's federation truststore and then becomes available as a CA Group on the policy graph. (Adding a CA restarts the federation server.)
  2. Give the server the hub's CA. Download the hub's ca.pem from the UI Settings → Download Self CA (or copy /opt/tak/federation-hub/certs/files/ca.pem). On the TAK Server, upload it under Configuration → Manage Federate Certificate Authorities so the server trusts the hub for federation.

Once both directions are in place, the two can authenticate; the policy then decides whether they actually exchange data.

Authorizing hub admins

The hub also uses X.509 client certs to authorize administrators (who may open the policy UI). Generate hub certs from /opt/tak/federation-hub/certs (makeRootCa.sh, makeCert.sh server <name>, makeCert.sh client <user>), then authorize an admin cert:

sudo su tak
java -jar /opt/tak/federation-hub/jars/federation-hub-manager.jar \
  /opt/tak/federation-hub/certs/files/<admin>.pem

This writes the admin to /opt/tak/federation-hub/authorized_users.yml (the location is referenced in federation-hub-ui.yml).

Optional: admin login via Keycloak

The hub UI can authenticate admins through Keycloak (OAuth) instead of/in addition to client certs — handy on a Deploy App deployment that already runs Keycloak. In federation-hub-ui.yml:

allowOauth: true
oauthPort: 9099
keycloakClaimName: groups        # token attribute to read
keycloakAdminClaimValue: admin   # value that grants admin
# keycloakServerName / keycloakClientId / keycloakSecret / endpoints …

So a user whose Keycloak token carries the admin group can administer the hub.

When mTLS isn't possible: token auth

On networks that break-and-inspect TLS, full mTLS can't work. The hub supports token (JWT) auth on a dedicated port (9103 by default). You enable it per-CA (Allow Token Auth on a CA Group node) or via a Token Group node whose tokens you distribute manually — both covered in Define the federation policy.
